messages:
julie_support: Filing an escalation — customer 'AcmeCorp' on Private VPC reporting intermittent 429s right after a nightly batch. Pattern: burst of ~800 req/s for ~4s then sustained 429s for ~10-20s. They say gateway logs show rate-limiter drops not upstream overload. Can infra advise on smoothing/tuning suggestions?

alex_enginfra: thx julie. can you paste the gateway and k8s ingress annotations they used? also which gateway version (we had a rate limiter change in 2025-11).

julie_support: gateway config snippet from customer below (sanitized):
```
# envoy rate limit config attached to gateway
ratelimit:
  mode: local
  token_bucket:
    capacity: 1000
    refill_rate: 50   # tokens/sec
    burst: 200
    ttl_seconds: 30
k8s_ingress_annotations:
  nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "10"
  nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "100"
  nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst-size: "50"
```
They also run a customer-managed gateway deployment with 2 replicas behind a load-balancer.

ken_runtime: quick read — refill_rate 50 and burst 200 -> able to absorb some bursts but your observed burst (~800/s) will exhaust the token bucket on each instance fast. When tokens are exhausted requests are 429'd until refill. With 2 replicas token bucket capacity is effectively per-replica unless they front with shared rate-limit service. Are they using local mode (yes) or remote RL service?

julie_support: they confirmed local (no centralized rate-limit service).

ken_runtime: ok. options: increase capacity/refill temporarily, or enable smoothing so bursts are spread across a short window. For on-prem private gateways we recommend one of three approaches: 
1) Centralized rate-limit service (Envoy external sob) so limits are global across replicas.
2) Increase per-replica token refill and capacity to match peak burst (e.g., capacity 2000, refill 400) but that raises sustained throughput and may expose upstream.
3) Use a short fronting queue + smoothing policy (leaky-bucket with small queue) so sudden client spikes are paced over ~5s.

alex_enginfra: also look at k8s side — ingress limit-rps only affects nginx side; if LB or external job fans out concurrently to both replicas you still get per-node buckets. If the batch job uses many client connections, suggest source-rate limiting at the client side (batch retry backoff) or implement request shaping on the customer side.

maria_sre: small pragmatic repro steps you can ask the customer to run so we see the pattern:
1) run this from an internal test pod adjacent to gateway: 
```
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -sS -X POST https://<gateway>/v1/infer -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' -d '{"input": "x"}' &
done
wait
```
2) capture gateway logs `kubectl -n gateway logs -l app=gateway --tail 200`
3) capture token-bucket metrics: `kubectl exec -it <gateway-pod> -- curl localhost:9090/metrics | grep token_bucket`

julie_support: customer ran a simplified repro and attached logs showing token bucket depletion and 429s. They don't have a central RL service and cannot add one immediately. They asked whether we support automatic short-term burst smoothing in the gateway config.

ken_runtime: we have a smoothing toggle in the gateway that uses a small request queue + adaptive drain; it's off by default in older installs. If they can't adopt central RL, recommend these edits:
```
ratelimit:
  mode: local
  token_bucket:
    capacity: 1500
    refill_rate: 300
    burst: 400
  smoothing:
    enabled: true
    max_queue_ms: 5000   # allow smoothing over 5s
    drain_rate_multiplier: 0.6
```
This will accept the burst into a short queue and drain tokens at a steadier rate so upstream sees traffic over a few seconds instead of a hard spike. Also reduce nginx limit-rps so it doesn't double-throttle.

alex_enginfra: FYI if they switch to smoothing we need to watch p99 latency and queue depth dashboards. add temporary alert: gateway.request_queue_depth > 100 for >2 minutes.

julie_support: relayed to customer. they asked about risk of spiky billing or upstream overload if we increase refill_rate.

ken_runtime: explain tradeoffs: raising refill/burst increases allowed instantaneous throughput -> could stress downstream model servers and increase token/billing usage during bursts. Smoothing tends to increase tail latency slightly but avoids mass 429s. If billing is a concern, pair smoothing with a short-term quota increase for specific API keys only during the nightly batch window (cron window policy).

maria_sre: additional quick mitigation: in k8s ingress add client-side connection limiting and keepalive tuning so the batch job cannot open hundreds of concurrent connections: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "20"` and set `keepalive: 100` on the client side.

julie_support: customer accepted plan: 1) enable smoothing with max_queue_ms 5000 2) increase capacity/refill modestly to {capacity:1500, refill_rate:300} 3) add cron window quota for batch API key 4) run repro test and share metrics. They'll roll out to a staging gateway first.

ops-bot: deploy-trigger: gateway-config-change detected for customer acmecorp (staging) — CI job queued.

alex_enginfra: I'll review the staging rollout and watch dashboards. If we see sustained queue growth we'll rollback to pre-change and advise adding a central RL service.

julie_support: closing this thread once staging proves healthy. will file a postmortem if any unexpected throttles remain. thanks all :thumbsup:
